To the extent that Manager has an opportunity to book a revenue-producing event on a date which is otherwise reserved for use by the Owner, Manager may propose alternative dates for the Owner’s event, and the Owner shall use best efforts to reschedule its event to allow Manager to book the revenue-producing event.
For purposes of calculating Manager’s Incentive Fee, Manager shall receive a “paper” credit for an amount equal to the difference between the published Facilities rate and the rate (if any) charged to the Owner for such use of the Facilities.
ARTICLE 6 PERSONNEL Section 6.1 General.
Other than the two (2) existing URI personnel assigned to the Center performing janitorial services, all Facility staff and other personnel shall be engaged or hired by Manager, and shall be employees, agents or independent contractors of Manager (or an Affiliate thereof), and not of the Owner.

Manager shall select, in its sole discretion but subject to Owner’s right to approve the Operating Budget, the number, function, qualifications, and compensation, including salary and benefits, of its employees and shall control the terms and conditions of employment (including without limitation termination thereof) relating to such employees.
Manager agrees to use reasonable and prudent judgment in the selection and supervision of such personnel, and will use its best efforts to recruit URI students, spouses of students and staff, and URI alumni.
The Owner specifically agrees that Manager shall be entitled to pay its employees, as an Operating Expense, bonuses and benefits in accordance with Manager’s then current employee manual, which may be modified by Manager from time to time in its sole discretion.
A copy of Manager’s current employee manual shall be provided to the Owner upon request.
Section 6.2 General Manager.
Personnel engaged by Manager will include an individual with managerial experience in similar facilities to serve as a full-time on-site General Manager of the Facilities.

Hiring of the General Manager by Manager shall require the prior approval of the Owner, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed; provided, however, in the event of a vacancy in the General Manager position, Manager may, upon notice to the Owner, temporarily fill such position with an interim General Manager for up to ninety (90) days without the necessity of obtaining the Owner’s approval.
The General Manager will have

11 4920-4464-0326.3 general supervisory responsibility for Manager and will be responsible for day-to-day operations of the Facilities, supervision of employees, and management and coordination of all activities associated with events taking place at the Facilities.
In the event that the General Manager plans to be absent from the facilities for more than five (5) consecutive calendar days for any reason, the General Manager shall so advise the Owner and shall indicate who shall be in charge during the General Manager’s absence.
Section 6.3 Non-Solicitation.
During the Term and for a period of one (1) year after the end of the Term, neither Owner nor any of its Affiliates shall solicit for employment any of Manager’s Management-Level Employees without Manager’s prior written approval.
In the event of a breach or anticipated breach of this Section by the Owner, Manager shall be entitled (in addition to any other rights and remedies which Manager may have at law or in equity, including money damages) to seek equitable relief, including an injunction to enjoin and restrain the Owner from continuing such breach, without the necessity of posting a bond.

ARTICLE 7 OPERATING BUDGET Section 7.1 Establishment of Operating Budget.
Attached hereto as Exhibit C is the Operating Budget for the 2025-2026 Operating Year, which Operating Budget is hereby approved by both Manager and Owner.
Manager agrees that at least 90 days prior (on or around April 1 st) to the commencement of each subsequent Operating Year in respect of such year, it will prepare and submit to the Owner its proposed Operating Budget for such year.
Each annual Operating Budget shall include Manager’s good faith projection of Revenues and Operating Expenses, presented on a monthly and annual basis, for the upcoming Operating Year.
The Owner agrees to provide Manager with all information in its possession necessary to enable Manager to prepare each Operating Budget.
Section 7.2 Approval of Operating Budget.
Each annual Operating Budget shall be subject to the review and approval of the Owner, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

In order for the Owner to fully evaluate and analyze such budgets or any other request by Manager relating to income and expenses, Manager agrees to provide to the Owner such reasonable financial information relating to the Facilities as may be requested by the Owner from time to time.
If extraordinary events occur during any Operating Year that could not reasonably be contemplated at the time the corresponding Operating Budget was prepared, Manager may submit an amendment to such budget for review and approval by the Owner (which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed).
If the Owner fails to approve any annual Operating Budget (or any proposed amendment thereto), the Owner shall promptly provide Manager the specific reasons therefor and its suggested modifications to Manager’s proposed Operating Budget or amendment in order to make it acceptable.

The parties shall then engage in good faith discussions and use reasonable commercial efforts to attempt to resolve the matter to the mutual satisfaction of the parties, including, if applicable, negotiation of a mutually acceptable modification to the economic terms of this Agreement to enable the Manager to achieve the compensation contemplated by its proposed Operating Budget.

12 4920-4464-0326.3 Section 7.3 Adherence to Operating Budget.
Manager shall use all reasonable efforts to manage and operate the Facilities in accordance with the Operating Budget.
However, Owner acknowledges that notwithstanding the Manager's experience and expertise in relation to the operation of facilities similar to the Facilities, the projections contained in each Operating Budget are subject to and may be affected by changes in financial, economic and other conditions and circumstances beyond the Manager’s control, and that Manager shall have no liability if the numbers within the Operating Budget are not achieved.
Manager agrees to notify the Owner within 30 days of any significant change or variance in the bottom line number in the Operating Budget, and any material increase in total Facility expenses from that provided for in the Operating Budget.
In either such case and if requested by Owner, Manager agrees to work with Owner to develop and implement a plan (or changes to the then current plan) to limit Operating Expense to be incurred in the remaining months of such Operating Year with the goal of achieving the Operating Budget.

ARTICLE 8 PROCEDURE FOR HANDLING INCOME Section 8.1 Event Account.
Manager shall deposit as soon as practical, upon receipt, but not less than once each business day, in the Event Account, all revenue received from ticket sales and similar event-related revenues which Manager receives in contemplation of, or arising from, an event, pending completion of the event.
Such monies will be held in escrow for the protection of ticket purchasers, the Owner, the Manager, and to provide a source of funds as required for payments to performers in connection with the presentation of events that must be paid prior to or contemporaneously with such events.
Promptly following completion of such event and settlement with Promoter, Manager shall transfer all funds remaining in the Event Account into the Operating Account.
Section 8.2 Operating Account.
Except as provided in Section 8.1, all Revenue and reimbursements (e.g., URI Athletic Box Office share) derived from operation of the Facilities shall be deposited by Manager into the Operating Account as soon as practical, upon receipt, but not less often than once each business day.

The specific procedures (and authorized individuals) for making deposits to and withdrawals from such account shall be set forth in the Operations Manual, but the parties specifically agree that Manager shall have authority to sign checks and make withdrawals from such account, subject to the limitations contained in this Agreement, without needing to obtain the co-signature of an Owner employee or representative.
Section 8.3 Event Marketing Fund Account.
Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in Sections 8.1 and 8.2, event income from an event for which funds from the Event Marketing Account were used as permitted herein shall be deposited by Manager into the Event Marketing Fund Account as soon as practical upon receipt, in the amount required to replenish the Event Marketing Fund Account up to its original balance of $250,000 only (excluding the additional contribution of $150,000 deposited in accordance with Section 9.3), with the remaining event income to be deposited into the Operating Account and considered to be Revenue.
In no event

13 4920-4464-0326.3 will the Event Marketing Fund Account exceed the $400,000 balance as of the date hereof, and in no event is Manager required to contribute any additional funds from its own account to the Fund, or otherwise to pay for any event losses or Operating Expenses with its own funds.
Further details for handling the Fund are provided in the Operations Manual, but in the event of any inconsistencies between this paragraph and the Operations Manual, the terms of this paragraph shall control.
ARTICLE 9 FUNDING Section 9.1 Source of Funding.
Manager shall pay all items of expense for the operation, maintenance, supervision and management of the Facilities from the funds in the Operating Account, which Manager may access for this purpose.
The Operating Account shall be funded with amounts generated by operation of the Facilities (as described in Article 8 above), or otherwise made available by the Owner.
To ensure sufficient funds are available in the Operating Account, Owner will deposit, or allow to remain, in the Operating Account, the amounts necessary to allow Manager to perform its obligations in accordance with the budgeted or otherwise approved Operating Expenses.

The Owner shall, upon request by Manager which requests shall be made three (3) times per Operating Year or on an as-needed basis following the Effective Date, deposit in the Operating Account the budgeted or otherwise approved expenses for funding needed.
Manager shall have no liability to the Owner or any third party in the event Manager is unable to perform its obligations hereunder, or under any third party contract entered into pursuant to the terms hereof, due to the fact that sufficient funds are not made available to Manager to pay such expenses in a timely manner.
Section 9.2 Advancement of Funds.
Under no circumstances shall Manager be required to pay for or advance any of its own funds to pay for any Operating Expenses.
In the event that, notwithstanding the foregoing, Manager agrees to advance its own funds to pay Operating Expenses, Owner shall promptly reimburse Manager for the full amount of such advanced funds, plus interest at a rate to be mutually agreed.
Section 9.3 Funding of Event Marketing Fund Account. (a) By no later than July 1, 2025, Manager will make a contribution to the Fund (as defined on Exhibit A) in the amount of $150,000 (the "Manager's Contribution").

The Fund will be utilized in accordance with Section 8.3 and as set forth in Exhibit A herein.
Should a balance remain at the end of the Term, any balance remaining in the Fund will belong to the Owner. (b) In the event of the termination of the Agreement prior to the five (5) year term (for any reason whatsoever, including without limitation if due to a breach, default or bankruptcy event by or affecting Manager), the Owner

14 4920-4464-0326.3 shall immediately pay to Manager the unamortized amount of Manager's Contribution as calculated herein.
The Manager's Contribution shall be amortized over a 5-year period starting on July 1, 2025 and ending on June 30, 2030, at the rate of $2,500 per month, and, in the event of the termination under this subsection (b), the amount due to Manager shall be equal to the Manager's Contribution reduced by $2,500 for each month elapsed from July 1, 2025 through the termination date.
ARTICLE 10 FISCAL RESPONSIBILITY; REPORTING Section 10.1 Records.
Manager agrees to keep and maintain, at its office in the Facilities, separate and independent records, in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, devoted exclusively to its operations in connection with its management of the Facilities.
Such records (including books, ledgers, journals, and accounts) shall contain all entries reflecting the business operations of Manager under this Agreement.
The Owner or its authorized agent shall have the right to audit and inspect such records from time to time during the Term, upon reasonable notice to Manager and during Manager's ordinary business hours.

This inspection of records will include providing the Owner view only role permissions of Manager’s accounting software programs.
Section 10.2 Monthly Financial Reports.
Manager agrees to provide to the Owner, within thirty (30) days after the end of each month during the Term, financial reports for the Facilities including a balance sheet, statement of cash flow, aging report on accounts receivable and accounts payable, and statement of revenues and expenditures (budget to actual) for such month and year to date in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.
In addition, Manager agrees to provide to the Owner a summary of bookings for each such month, and separate cash receipts and disbursements reports for each event held at the Facilities during such month.
Additionally, Manager shall submit to the Owner, on a monthly basis, copies of all bank statements and reconciliations concerning the Event Account and the Operating Account.
Section 10.3 Agreed-Upon Procedures.

Manager agrees to use reasonable commercial efforts to provide to the Owner, within one hundred and twenty (120) days following the end of each Operating Year, an Independent Accountant’s Report on Applying Agreed-Upon Procedures.
This attestation engagement will be performed by an external auditor, approved by the Owner, and shall be conducted in accordance with attestation standards established by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants.
Such procedures, developed and agreed upon by the Owner and Manager, when performed and reported on by an independent practitioner, will provide assurance that the financial statements and procedures are sufficient and comply with the applicable reporting framework per this Agreement.

15 4920-4464-0326.3 Costs associated with obtaining such an attestation report shall be an Operating Expense of the Facilities.
ARTICLE 11 CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS Section 11.1 Schedule of Capital Expenditures.
Manager shall annually, at the time of submission of the annual Operating Budget to the Owner, provide to the Owner a schedule of proposed capital improvements to be made at the Facilities, for the purpose of allowing the Owner to consider such projects and to prepare and update a long-range Capital Expenditure budget.
Section 11.2 Responsibility for Capital Expenditures.
The Owner shall be solely responsible for all Capital Expenditures at the Facilities; provided, however, the Owner shall be under no obligation to make any Capital Expenditures proposed by Manager, and provided further that Manager shall have no liability for any claims, costs or damages arising out of a failure by the Owner to make any Capital Expenditures.
Notwithstanding the foregoing, Manager shall have the right (but not the obligation), upon notice to the Owner, to make Capital Expenditures at the Facilities for Emergency Repairs.

In such event, the Owner shall promptly reimburse Manager for the cost of such Capital Expenditure.
Further details are provided in the Operations Manual.
ARTICLE 12 FACILITY CONTRACTS; TRANSACTIONS WITH AFFILIATES Section 12.1 Existing Contracts.
The Owner shall provide to Manager, on or before the Effective Date, copies of all Existing Contracts except for event contracts.
Manager shall administer and assure compliance with such Existing Contracts as well as the event contracts.
Section 12.2 Execution of Contracts.
Manager shall have the right to enter into Service Contracts, Revenue Generating Contracts and other contracts related to the operation of the Facilities, as agent on behalf of the Owner.
Any such material agreements shall contain standard indemnification and insurance obligations on the part of each vendor, licensee or service provider, as is customary for the type of services or obligations being provided or performed by such parties.

Manager shall obtain the prior approval of the Owner (which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed) before entering into any such contract with a term that expires after the Term of this Agreement, unless such contract, by its express terms, can be terminated by Manager or Owner following expiration of the Term without any penalty.
Section 12.3 Transactions with Affiliates.
In connection with its obligations hereunder relating to the purchase or procurement of services for the Facilities (including without limitation food and beverage services, ticketing services, Commercial Rights sales, web design services and graphic design services), Manager may purchase or procure such services, or otherwise transact business with, an Affiliate of Manager, provided that the prices charged and services rendered by such Affiliate are competitive with those obtainable from any unrelated parties rendering comparable services.
Manager shall, at the request of the Owner, provide reasonable evidence

16 4920-4464-0326.3 establishing the competitive nature of such prices and services, including, if appropriate, competitive bids from other persons seeking to render such services at the Facilities.

Each party shall appoint a contract administrator who shall monitor such party’s compliance with the terms of this Agreement.
Manager’s contract administrator shall be its General Manager at the Facilities, unless Manager notifies Owner of a substitute contract administrator in writing.
Owner’s Contract Administrator shall be the Vice President for Administration and Finance or his/her designee.

ARTICLE 15 INSURANCE Section 15.1 Types and Amount of Coverage.
Manager agrees to obtain insurance coverage in the manner and amounts as set forth in Exhibit D, attached hereto, and shall provide to the Owner promptly following the Effective Date a certificate of certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage.

Manager shall require that all third-party users of the Facilities, including without limitation third-party licensees, ushers, security personnel and concessionaires, provide certificates of insurance evidencing insurance appropriate for the types of activities in which such user is engaged.

If Manager subcontracts any of its obligations under this Agreement, Manager shall require each such subcontractor to secure insurance that will protect against applicable hazards or risks of loss as and in the minimum amounts designated herein, and name Manager and the Owner as additional insureds.

(a) Neither party shall be liable or responsible to the other party for any delay, loss, damage, failure or inability to perform under this Agreement due to an Event of Force Majeure, provided that the party claiming failure or inability to perform provides written notice to the other party within thirty (30) days of the date on which such party gains actual knowledge of such Event of Force Majeure.

Proc. 2017-13 as amended, modified or replaced from time to time (the “Rev.

TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Finance and Facilities Committee FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: June 26, 2025 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of the Certain Documents Relative to the Development, Construction, and Financing of New University Housing Purpose of Submittal: To recommend the Board of Trustees Finance and Facilities Committee recommend approval to the Board of Trustees of the New University Housing (NUH) Project and authorize execution of documents for the development, construction, and financing of two new on-campus undergraduate student housing communities and one graduate student and family housing community at the University of Rhode Island.
Background: In late 2022, the University of Rhode Island engaged a planning team led by Scion Advisory Services, with architects from CannonDesign, to develop a Housing and Residential Life Housing Master Plan to transform URI housing.

This initiative aligned with URI’s strateg ic commitment to enhance t he student experience by providing modern, affordable, and desirable livin g spaces.
The plan recommended that URI pursue a public-private-partnership (P3) to address immediate housing needs on the Kingston campus.
In May 2024, URI issued a public request for proposal for a development partner, and after a thorough vetting process, selected Gilbane Development Company (Gilbane) as its P3 partner.
In September 2024, the University entered into a Preliminary Development Agreement (PDA) with Gilbane.
In March 2025, the University approved the feasibility study conducted by Gilbane confirming that the project was feasible and would move forward.
Gilbane then selected, with URI’s concurrence, Provident to serve as the project 501(c)(3) partner.
PRG – RI Properties LLC, a single member limited liability company, was organized by Provident for the Project.
URI DevCo LLC, a single purpose subsidiary of Gilbane, was also organized for development of the Project.

In April 2025, URI DevCo, Provident, and Raymond James (underwriter) commenced the application process to issue debt through the Rhode Island Health and Education Building Corporation (RIHEBC).
The Project is summarized below.
Project Overview: Project Scope & Design: x Total Beds: 1,134 x Planned Housing Phases: o Occupancy in Fall 2027: 514 undergraduate beds o Occupancy in Fall 2028: 400 undergraduate beds o Occupancy in Fall 2028: 220 graduate beds

x Building Types: o Undergraduate Housing (Two Buildings): Apartment-style, single bedrooms in two- and four- bedroom units.
Modular construction. o Graduate Housing (Six Buildings + Community Center): Apartments with studio, one-bedroom, two-bedroom, and three-bedroom configurations.
Modular rebuild on existing foundations. o All buildings meet state code and URI design standards.
Financial Summary (rounded): x Total Project Cost: $231MM (as of June 2025). x URI Equity Contribution: The University may fund an equity contribution to the Project, the amount of which is currently subject to negotiation, and will be up to the amount authorized by the Board during executive session. x Rental Rates: Rental rates are within acceptable range to URI Housing and Residential Life, though may need to increase due to changes in market conditions. x Annual Rate Escalation: 3% x Expected Occupancy Rate: 95% x Debt Term: 40 years (all-in). x Debt Coverage Ratio: 1.2x or better (Senior Debt). x Residual Cash Flow to URI: $317MM over the term (NPV @ 5% = $63.7MM).

Document Approval Over the past several months, the University has negotiated and vetted several Project documents, three of which are being brought to the Board today for approval, and two of which are being shared for informational purposes.

These documents, listed below, are described in more detail in the enclosed Board of Trustees resolutions. x The Ground Lease between the University and the Provident, will extend for a term of up to 42 years and will contain provisions requiring the Project to be constructed in accordance with campus standards (for approval). x The Affiliation Agreement between the University and Provident, which outlines each entity’s obligations to the project (for approval). x The Interim Management Agreement between the University and URI DevCo LLC, which will allow the University to continue to manage the graduate student housing until the expected turnover date of May 2026, at which time it will be turned over to th e Developer for demolition and re-construction (for approval). x The Turnkey Development Agreement between URI DevCo LLC and Provident, pursuant to which the Developer will implement the design, construction, and commissioning of the Project for a stipulated sum in accordance with plans approved by the University (for information). x The Project Management Agreement between Provident and In wood Management, outlining operations and maintenance of the Student Housing Facilities (for information).

Next Steps Upon the Board’s approval of the Project and authorization to continue negotiating required documents, URI will finalize the negotiation and execute the relevant documents.
The Project is scheduled for financial close in September 2025, at which point the final Project budget will be determined.
We look forward to continued collaboration with Gilbane to ensure this critical project’s seamless and successful implementation.

Public-Private Partnership Project Summary and Scope The Project is structured as a concession agreement with a private qualified development firm to enter into a public-private partnership (“ P3”), which requires a ground lease for the structure and the issuance of bonds by the Rhode Island Health and Educational Building Corporation (the “ Issuer”).
This P3 is a delivery approa ch, whereby, when appropriate and feasible, the University can utilize the P3 model to secure the anticipated advantages of increased speed of delivery, guaranteed maximum price and firm delivery date, and sh aring risk with the private sector.
In a P3 model, the University leases its land to a tax-exempt nonprofit entity in the form of a ground lease.
That entity engages the developer and contractors to construct the buildings.
The nonprofit entity owns the buildings until the debt is retired.
At that time, ownership reverts to the University, and the ground lease terminates.

Project Structure, Financing and Document Package The total cost of the Project is currently estimated to be approximately $231M, which is expected to be financed through the bond issuance by the Issuer.
The proceeds of the bonds will be loaned by the Issuer to the Lessee/Borrower.
The University may also fund an equity contribution, the amount of which is currently subject to negotiation and will be up to the amount authorized by the Board during executive session.
The proposed financing structure for the Project will be based on a privatized P3 financing model through which the Board will ground lease the land on which the Project is located to the Lessee/Borrower.

The Ground Lease for the Project between the University and the Lessee/Borrower (the “Ground Lease”) will extend for a term of up to 42 years, which will be in excess of the maturity of the proposed bond financing, and will contain provisions requiring the Project to be constructed in accordance with campus standards.
Provisions in the Ground Lease and Affiliation Agreement will also include certain areas of support and c ooperation between the University and the Lessee/Borrower.
Under the Ground Lease, the land will always remain owned by the University, and the Lessee/Borrower will own the Student Housing Facilities for the term of the financing.
